findings.text: All 7 acceptance criteria are testable and map to concrete user actions: file format/size validation (AC-1), dimension validation (AC-2), S3 upload + DB linkage (AC-3), duplicate replacement (AC-4), deletion (AC-5), mobile pickers (AC-6), web drag-drop + input (AC-7).
Data flows documented in 7-step pipeline: file selection → validation (format, size, dimensions) → S3 upload → DB update → confirmation. Each step identifies source, data, and validation rules.

7 domain rules enforced: file format whitelist (JPG/PNG only), 5 MB hard limit, 100×100 minimum pixels, single active image per user, S3 object lifecycle, private ACL, platform-specific UI. All rules specify enforcement mechanism.

7 edge cases identified with mitigations: concurrent uploads (button disable + row lock), S3 success + DB failure (compensating rollback), S3 delete fails + DB cleared (async cleanup), corrupted image header, unauthorized access, disk exhaustion, extension/MIME mismatch.

5 open questions require PO/stakeholder input: image resizing, S3 region/bucket/CDN strategy, soft delete vs permanent deletion, upload timeout/progress UI, multiple image sizes. These do not block phase 2; architect will document assumptions.

6 assumptions documented: S3 bucket pre-provisioned, user authentication in place, users table has profile_image_url column, mobile apps can make HTTPS requests, image dimension extraction via library, no payment/PII involved.

decisions: Story BASELINE-002 is a synthetic test case for token usage measurement across 10 pipeline phases.
Platform scope: iOS (native picker), Android (native picker), Web (drag-drop + file input) all feed same validation and S3 upload pipeline.
S3 storage pattern: users/{userId}/profile.{ext}; single active image per user with atomic replacement on re-upload.
Image validation: format (JPG/PNG), size (<=5MB), dimensions (>=100x100) applied before S3 upload.
Error cases: S3 failure compensated by rollback; orphaned S3 objects resolved by async cleanup job.
